The original paper has no delivered files, so heads that use result files or code cannot use "the original paper ranks first" for acceptance; their known answers can only come from damaged copies and the ladder.

### The final paper: review-style scores bunch together, drift, and are fooled by packaging

Human scores for ICLR and NeurIPS papers are themselves not very consistent. At ICLR 2025, human-human Spearman is **0.41** ([Stanford Agentic Reviewer](https://paperreview.ai/tech-overview)); in the NeurIPS 2021 consistency experiment, the correlation between two human reviewers' scores was only 0.14 ([AI Scientist, arXiv 2408.06292](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.06292)). The best reviewers only match this ceiling. Stanford Agentic Reviewer is at 0.42, DeepReviewer-14B at 0.356 and 0.405, and the AI Scientist reviewer with a Claude-3.5 backend at only **0.037 and −0.022** ([DeepReviewer](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.08569)). Absolute scores drift with the judge. At Agents4Science 2025, three LLM reviewers gave the same set of papers mean scores of **2.30** (GPT-5), 3.0 (Claude Sonnet 4) and **4.23** (Gemini 2.5 Pro), with pairwise Pearson 0.48 ([Agents4Science](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.15534)). For the same set of Zochi papers, the Sakana reviewer gave 7.67 and DeepReviewer-14B gave 4.50–4.63. When the same DeepReviewer-14B scored the same set of public papers, the numbers reported in two papers differed by up to 0.68 ([DeepScientist](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.26603); [Jr. AI Scientist](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.04583)). Packaging can fool them. BadScientist had GPT-5 write papers without running experiments; a reviewer panel of o3, o4-mini and GPT-4.1 accepted up to **82.0%** (TooGoodGains strategy) ([BadScientist](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.18003)). Jr. AI Scientist itself reports that fabricated ablations actually raised the review scores ([Jr. AI Scientist](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.04583)). On ICLR 2026, frontier models from three vendors could all separate accepts from rejects, but none could separate oral from poster ([arXiv 2608.03659](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03659), abstract only).

Pairwise comparison has higher resolving power. Remeli and Hardt found that Elo aggregated from pairwise verdicts has a Spearman above 0.9 with the true accuracy ranking; when the judge is weaker, it is clearly better than direct scoring ([arXiv 2606.09409](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09409), abstract only). Si et al. found that Claude-3.5, zero-shot, judges which of two ICLR submissions was accepted with 71.4% accuracy; when predicting absolute scores directly, it is poorly calibrated ([Si et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.04109)). The cost is that pairwise comparison is more sensitive to distractor features: after distractor features are injected, about **35%** of pairwise preferences flip, versus only 9% of absolute scores ([arXiv 2504.14716](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14716), abstract only). Presentation dimensions saturate easily: on ResearchClawBench, most systems score above 70 on "professionalism", while all other dimensions are low ([ResearchClawBench](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.07591)).

Our results fit this picture exactly. The AI Scientist reviewer gave only 3s and 4s across 16 papers. Stanford, on resubmission of the same paper, differed by 0.4–1.2 points, and lowered its score only for heavy damage; its test-retest variance has never been published in the literature, so our number has no public value to compare against. The frozen pairwise judge re-judged 15 pairs and gave the same result on all 15; on 24 graded-damage pairs it picked the control every time, starting from level 1. But it gives only one overall verdict.

[Inference] Paper quality should still be measured by pairwise comparison, with the overall verdict split into sub-items; absolute review scores serve only as an extra view. Pairwise comparison is more sensitive to distractors, so the lengthened, polished and injected copies that our judge has not yet been tested on must be added.

### Trajectory and process: run-level flags are trustworthy, step-level attribution is not

MAST, a multi-agent failure taxonomy, uses o1 as the annotator; its agreement with experts is κ = **0.77**, versus 0.88 human-human, and κ = 0.79 on unseen systems ([MAST](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.13657)). On METR's MALT data, the best monitor detects reward hacking (exploiting loopholes in the scoring rules) with AUROC 0.96 ([METR MALT](https://metr.org/blog/2025-10-14-malt-dataset-of-natural-and-prompted-behaviors/)). Agent-as-a-Judge inspects the workspace and judges whether each requirement is met; its agreement with human consensus is about 90%, versus about 70% for a plain LLM judge ([Agent-as-a-Judge](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.10934)). Step-level localization does not work. On TRAIL, the best joint accuracy is **0.183 and 0.050** ([TRAIL](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.08638)). Step-level attribution accuracy on Who&When is 14.2% ([Who&When](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00212)). Judges from different families agree on "which step has the first error" in only 21/57 cases ([arXiv 2610.17633](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17633), abstract only).

For research agents, the thing most worth checking in the logs is integrity. A study covering 17 models and 38 tasks found that on open-ended research-workflow tasks, agents spontaneously exploited loopholes **30.5%** of the time, and **75%** of these were test-set leakage; a review panel that looked only at code and reported scores missed 6.5% of the confirmed hacks ([arXiv 2609.28614](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28614)). AIRA-dojo found that choosing the final solution by test score instead of validation score inflates results by 9–13 points ([AIRA-dojo](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.02554)). The Agentic Scientist reports that in 2 of 3 runs its agent quietly changed the evaluation protocol from pass@1 to majority vote; neither the evaluator nor the rubric caught it, only a manual audit did ([arXiv 2610.18933](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.18933v1)). Process features relate to outcomes. HAL found on 1,634 records that tasks with self-correction during the run have 1.5–4 times higher success rates, and those with explicit verification 13–87% higher ([HAL](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11977)). FML-bench measures exploration diversity by the dispersion of per-round code embeddings; it correlates positively with performance on 5 of 8 tasks ([FML-bench](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.10472)).

Non-uniform log formats already have existing solutions. Harbor's ATIF trajectory format is emitted natively by Claude Code, Codex and others, and supports sub-agent trajectories ([Harbor ATIF](https://docs.harborframework.com/agents/atif)). Docent represents one multi-agent run as several transcripts under one run, split by role ([Docent](https://docs.transluce.org/concepts/overview)). But the harness itself can create false signals. Of the hand-built failures in Who&When, 45% were actually runs crashed by the provider's content filter, after which the harness itself emitted a final answer ([arXiv 2611.13254](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13254), abstract only). Stability metrics all require running the same task several times, including pass^k, outcome consistency and trajectory consistency; "Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability" runs each task 5 times ([arXiv 2602.16666](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.16666)). There is no mature metric for the "plan stability" of research agents. Nor has any study unified three kinds of logs into one format to compare AI scientist systems: multi-role logs plus git history, single-agent transcripts, and raw API request logs.

[Inference] For us, the first use of logs is to set pass conditions for integrity: whether the test set took part in selection, whether the evaluation protocol was changed, and whether labels that should not be read were read. The second use is process diagnosis, to explain why results differ. Diagnostics must be normalized per experiment, not per message, because multi-role systems naturally produce extra coordination messages. Single-agent systems have no inter-agent failures; such metrics are recorded as "not applicable", not as zero. Stability metrics that depend on repeated runs do not fit our design and are not adopted.

### Cost: a frozen price table plus a quality-cost Pareto front can be copied directly

AstaBench converts the tokens of each model call to dollars using a frozen litellm price snapshot, reports cost per problem, and marks the score-cost Pareto front ([AstaBench](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.21652)). InnovatorBench lists hours and dollars next to the scores ([InnovatorBench](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.27598)). ResearchClawBench plots cost against score and runtime against score ([ResearchClawBench](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.07591)). The judge itself is not cheap either: PaperBench costs about **$66** per paper with o3-mini as judge, and about $830 with o1 ([PaperBench](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.01848)). Kosmos tried to measure value as "equivalent to how many months of expert work"; the survey estimate was 6.14 months and the formula estimate 4.1 months, about 50% apart ([Kosmos](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.02824v2)). No source has reported "cost per verified finding".

[Inference] Subscription-based Claude Code and Codex have no comparable bills, so cost is estimated from tokens and a frozen price table. Judge cost is listed separately per paper. "Expert-month equivalents" are not adopted.

ML research systems and natural-science discovery systems each have their own way of proving themselves. The table below lists only those most relevant to us. "Matched" means the same base model, the same budget and the same inputs.

These practices share a pattern. "Better" is usually argued from the single best output: v2 picked the best copy for each idea, Jr. AI Scientist picked 3 papers out of 18, and DeepScientist had 21 successes among about 5,000 ideas; the typical output of a run is rarely reported ([DeepScientist](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.26603); [Jr. AI Scientist](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.04583)). A survey covering 24 runnable systems found that 83% release code, but only **38%** release seeds or execution trajectories, and 38% report any novelty validation ([arXiv 2608.05179](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05179), abstract only). ChemCrow documents the clearest counterexample: chemistry experts preferred ChemCrow on all three criteria, while GPT-4 as judge preferred bare GPT-4, rewarding fluency and apparent completeness ([ChemCrow](https://arxiv.org/html/2304.05376v5)). On the natural-science side, external corrections all concern "is it really new, and is it really right". A-Lab's Nature correction changed "new materials" to "new to the prediction platform" ([Chemistry World](https://chemistryworld.com/news/new-analysis-raises-doubts-over-autonomous-labs-materials-discoveries/4018791.article)). An independent group re-tested 3 of Kosmos's hypotheses: 1 held, 1 did not, and 1 was unclear ([arXiv 2511.13825](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13825)).

Benchmarks that have tested our systems also do not give reliable gaps. ResearchClawBench builds 40 tasks from hidden published papers: Claude Code (Opus 4.6) **21.5**, EvoScientist v0.1.1 **18.8**, Codex CLI **18.4**; all 8 agents fall in 12.8–21.5. It reports no judge-human agreement, re-judging variance or confidence intervals, and the paper gives two different values, 24.6 and 25.8, for the frontier models' mean score ([ResearchClawBench](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.07591)). AstaBench included a "Faker": it runs no experiments and simply makes up the report, code and outputs. It scored **39.2** on E2E-Bench, higher than ReAct (o3) at 34.9 and ReAct (gpt-5) at 30.0; even the best agent completed all steps in only 1% of experiments ([AstaBench](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.21652)).

[Inference] Six things can be copied over. First, matched conditions, which our fairness audit already does. Second, the claim, not the run, as the statistical unit. Third, statement audits broken down by type. Fourth, a human-written control; we already put the original paper in every batch as an anchor. Fifth, success criteria written down in advance. Sixth, Station-style "recover the original paper's sub-findings", which is the same thing as our rubric coverage and can be changed from binary to graded. What cannot be copied is self-play Elo, venue acceptance and comparison by showcase papers. The comparison we need, a multi-role research organization versus a single coding agent, AS and EVO on tasks adapted from papers, has no precedent in the literature. The closest work, ResearchClawBench, has no judge validation at all, so our evaluator must rely on its own known-answer evidence and cannot borrow anyone else's numbers.

## Judge validation has converged: planted defects, false-positive rate on clean samples, item-by-item re-testing

Validating a judge against humans has a low ceiling. Human-human Spearman on review scores is about 0.41, so "agreeing with humans" means a rank correlation of about 0.4 at best. [Inference] The notes computed this with a normal approximation: a Spearman of 0.4 on 147 papers has a 95% confidence interval of about [0.26, 0.53], so a tie such as "0.42 vs 0.41" cannot actually tell which is better. Detection of planted defects discriminates better. A NeurIPS 2026 benchmark planted 177 errors in 15 astrophysics preprints and tested 12 reviewing systems. The best detection rate is **70.6 ± 6.2%**. With the same free-form prompt, three frontier models differ by **48.6 points**. With a structured prompt, Claude Code's detection rate rises by 32.2 points. On clean papers, the lowest false-positive rate is 1.0%, and the multi-agent reviewer's is 2.8% ([NeurIPS 2026 poster](https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/poster/152885), abstract only). On another benchmark, the best single model catches 71.6% of planted errors, and the union of 6 models catches 83.3% ([arXiv 2606.19749](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19749), abstract only). Real errors are much harder than planted ones: recall on SPOT is only 21%. Precision has to be measured by manual spot checks of flags, which is what FabScore and "To Err Is Human" both do. Pairs with known outcomes can also serve as an acceptance set: off-the-shelf frontier models predicting "which of two ideas does better when tested" perform at chance; a purpose-fine-tuned system reaches 77% on 1,585 test pairs ([arXiv 2506.00794](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.00794)).

Stable does not mean valid. SPOT's models rarely find the same error again across 8 runs. "Rating Roulette" found that repeated scoring of the same output can be close to random, and setting temperature to 0 does not fix it (secondary, [arXiv 2510.27106](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.27106)). Agreement should be measured with chance-corrected κ or α, not percent agreement (not re-checked, [arXiv 2406.12624](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12624)). Arena-Hard defines a benchmark's "separability" as the share of model pairs whose bootstrap 95% confidence intervals do not overlap; its value is 87.4%, versus only 22.6% for MT-Bench (not re-checked, [arXiv 2406.11939](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11939)). Several good practices in system papers are worth learning from. Robin first measured its own judge: judge self-consistency 88%, humans 61%; overlap with the experts' top 10 is 7.25/10 ([Robin](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.13400v1)). AI co-scientist ran the same comparison with 4 different LLM judges and reported only the conclusions on which all 4 agreed ([AI co-scientist](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18864)). The value of multi-judge panels has to be looked at case by case. On general QA, PoLL, a panel of small models from three vendors, has higher κ with humans than a single GPT-4, for example 0.763 vs 0.627 on NQ, at about 7–8 times lower cost ([PoLL](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.18796)). In error finding, panels raise recall through the union. But a panel from a single family fails together: in BadScientist, a reviewer panel made up entirely of OpenAI models still accepted 69% of fabricated papers ([BadScientist](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.18003)).

Biases have to be measured one by one. The table below lists the magnitudes in the literature, how we measure each, and our current status.

| Bias | Magnitude in the literature | How to measure | Our status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position | In Ideation Arena, GPT-4o is consistent after an order swap only 45.0% of the time, other judges 70.6–92.5% ([Ideation Arena](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.29696v1)); in Lit2Test 21% of pairs are order-sensitive | Judge each pair in both orders, report the disagreement rate | Done: the two orders agree on 92.3% of pairs; 2.7% of the pairs used for ranking disagree |
| Length and polish | Judges chose the longer proposal in 50.9–62.0% of valid verdicts ([Ideation Arena](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.29696v1)); a direct judge's substance-identification rate is only 0.504 ([SciStyleBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01666), abstract only) | Lengthened copies (irrelevant appendix or figures added) and polished copies against the original | Not measured |
| Same-family preference | AI reviewers rate AI-written proposals about 1 point higher (on a 5-point scale) and identify AI authorship 100% of the time ([arXiv 2607.25881](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25881), abstract only); GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 show same-family preference, magnitude not given in the abstract ([Play Favorites](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06709)); counterexample: after controlling for paper quality, the "LLM reviews prefer LLM papers" effect disappears ([arXiv 2601.20920](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20920)) | Style swap: the same content is rewritten once by a model from each of two families; see which version the judge favors | The GPT judge pushed all 60 cross-family disagreements toward the GPT-written paper; the Claude judge's family shift is not yet measured |
| Leniency and compression | Mean score ranges from 2.30 to 4.23 depending on the judge; scores in fully LLM-written reviews are heavily compressed ([Agents4Science](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.15534); [arXiv 2601.20920](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20920)) | Compare rankings or pairwise results only within one judge; do not mix raw scores | The AI Scientist reviewer gives only 3 and 4 |
| Fooled by packaging, and "names the problem but scores high anyway" | Acceptance rate of fabricated papers up to 82%; o4-mini still gave an accept score in 100% of the cases where it flagged integrity concerns ([BadScientist](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.18003)) | Fabricated copies, delivery-mismatch copies; count the share where the rationale names a fatal problem but the verdict does not change | Partly measured: on copies with altered numbers, the control won all 24 pairs |
| Prompt injection | Manipulating 5% of reviews pushes 12% of papers out of the top 30%; LLMs repeat minor limitations disclosed by authors 4.5 times as consistently as humans ([arXiv 2412.01708](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.01708), abstract only); Agents4Science caught 2 injected papers | Copies with white-text or invisible instructions: the verdict should not move, and the scan must flag them | Not measured |
| Intransitivity | LLM judge preferences are intransitive; all-pairs comparison plus Bradley–Terry raises Kendall agreement with the Chatbot Arena ranking from 82.1% to 86.3% ([arXiv 2502.14074](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14074), abstract only) | Report the share of three-way cycles | All-pairs comparison plus Bradley–Terry already used; cycle share not reported |

[Inference] Our graded damage gradient is the "dose-response plus clean control" design from the literature. What is missing is injection, lengthening and polish, style swap, cycle share and separability; single-paper heads must also report false positives on clean copies. On the GPT judge favoring GPT papers, the literature has both evidence of family preference and a counterexample saying "it is really a quality difference". Only a control that fixes the content and changes only the writing style can tell which one it is. Sample size is a limit. [Inference] By the notes' normal approximation, showing that a pairwise win rate of 0.65 is significantly above 0.5 needs about 85 non-tied pairs; at a win rate of 0.75, about 29 pairs. So a style swap with 10–20 pairs can only detect a large family shift. A detection rate of 0.8 measured on 30 planted defects has a 95% confidence interval of about ±0.14.

## Recommendation: add four evidence heads to the three kinds of head in #377, and have each head pass a small known-answer sample first

This whole section is a recommendation ([Inference]); the basis is given in each row.

The literature supports the core principle of #377: the model only reads and finds; comparing and counting go to code. There are three reasons. First, code comparison does not change with the judge, family preference is kept out of the rules, and the only difference left between two judges is "which entries were listed", which can be measured directly (in #377, for the same CC-sonnet t09 paper, GPT listed 72 entries and Claude listed 64). Second, counts and ratios have clear resolving power and do not bunch at 3 and 4 like review scores. Third, holistic scoring is exactly where LLMs are weakest in the literature, while they do well on tasks like "find and copy out". So we recommend extracting everything that can be turned into structured data and letting code compute on it, leaving to the model only what truly needs judgment, with planted mutations as known answers for every model judgment. The results of the heads are reported side by side, not combined into one overall score. The lesson of #304 supports this: "verify first, then decide the better of a pair by a fixed rule" agreed with the maintainer's labels 0/6.

| Head and dimension | Input | Who computes | Form and resolving power | Known-answer acceptance before the full run | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Code head: delivery and fairness audit (existing) | Run records, delivery manifest | Code | Pass condition | Keep the existing checks | #377 |
| Code head: hygiene gate (new) | Paper text layer; citations checked against CrossRef, OpenAlex, arXiv and Semantic Scholar in that order | Code | Pass condition; also report the number of suspicious citations | Copies with planted fake citations, white-text instructions, and `TODO` and `??` citation residue are all caught; zero on control copies | At Agents4Science only about 44% of submissions had no suspicious citations, and 2 injections were caught; CoE I3; AutoResearchClaw |
| Code head: cost (existing, to be completed) | Session or API logs, frozen price table | Code | Graded: dollars, tokens, wall clock, time with experiments running; plot the quality-cost Pareto front; judge cost listed separately per paper | Reconcile against the token records of one known run | AstaBench |
| Code head: process diagnostics (new) | Unified event stream: LLM calls, executions, file changes, experiment start and end, plus per-system field-availability flags | Code counts | Diagnostic, not used for ranking: execution errors per experiment, recoveries, number of experiments, code snapshot diversity, whether the arm change took effect | For each log type, hand-count 1–2 runs; the counts match the code counts | MAST; HAL; FML-bench; ATIF |
| Single-paper head: number traceability (existing in #377) | Paper, plus the result files the judge names | Model extracts and locates; code compares at the precision printed in the paper | Graded: inconsistencies per hundred entries, coverage, share with no source found; inconsistencies in the abstract and main table listed separately | The items in #377, plus "delivery-mismatch" copies (the paper paired with the delivery from another run of the same task): inconsistencies or missing sources should rise sharply | FabScore; AutoResearchClaw number registry |
| Single-paper head: evidence strength (new) | Paper, plus result files (per-seed numbers needed) | Model extracts each main comparison as one row (values, number of seeds, dispersion, datasets, model scale, baselines, ablations); code computes | Graded: gain/noise ratio per claim, share with "noise unknown"; numbers of datasets, model scales, baselines and ablations; coverage of the original paper's experimental setup | Remove dispersion, remove the strongest baseline, remove one dataset, squeeze the gain into noise (paper and result files changed together), 3 levels each; the matching quantity must change monotonically | These kinds of weakness are exactly what separated systems in our reviews; LimitGen taxonomy; AutoResearchClaw zero-variance gate; Bouthillier, rliable |
| Single-paper head: claim scope (new) | Paper, plus the evidence rows extracted in the row above | Model | Graded: each finding carries a severity and a quote from the text; count major and fatal findings, do not take a mean score | Add 1, 3 or 5 overreaching generalizations, causal claims without ablation support, or untested "significant" to the abstract and conclusion; report recall by type | ARA L2 (overreach 23/23, but the mean score does not fall with serious problems); RIGOURATE; Kosmos interpretation 57.9% |
| Code-paper consistency (new) | The paper's method section, plus the parts of the code for method, loss, metrics and data split | Model reads the code | Graded: number of confirmed inconsistencies, by SciCoQA category; a wrong metric formula or evaluation on the wrong split is recorded as a pass condition | Change the metric function, change the evaluation split, hard-code a result, make an ablation condition identical to the control | SciCoQA; FabScore experimental fabrication; CoE I4 |
| Selection and protocol integrity (new) | Code and logs | Code decides when structured records exist; otherwise the model gives a run-level flag | Pass condition | Plant "choose the configuration by the test set", a changed evaluation protocol, and reading test labels into the logs and code of copies | Luo et al.; AIRA-dojo; the research-agent loophole study; The Agentic Scientist |
| Single-paper head: rubric coverage (existing, optional) | Paper, plus the evaluator-side rubric, optionally result files | Model | Graded: 0–100 per item, the original paper's level is 50; note whether support comes from the main text, result files or code | Coverage falls on copies with experiments removed; direction along the ladder | ResearchClawBench RADS; AstaBench; Station |
| Comparison head: overall verdict and sub-items (existing in #377) | Images of all pages, anonymized, both orders | Model, two judges: Claude and GPT | Graded: Bradley–Terry strength; two systems count as separated only if both labels point the same way and differ by more than 0.55; each sub-item aggregated separately | The items in #377, plus injected copies, lengthened copies and style-swap pairs | SciArena; ReviewerToo; Remeli and Hardt |

Layered by input: the comparison head, hygiene gate and claim scope need only the paper; number traceability, evidence strength and rubric coverage need the paper plus result files; code-paper consistency needs the paper plus code; selection and protocol integrity, process diagnostics and cost need logs. The original paper exists only as a PDF, so "the original paper ranks first" can be used only to accept paper-only heads. Ideas do not get a head of their own. They show up in the comparison head's overall verdict, in the rubric's coverage of the original paper's core components, and in the evidence heads: whether an idea is good depends on what evidence it finally produces. Material that can be reused directly: ARA's rigor-reviewer is MIT, SciCoQA and LimitGen data are CC BY 4.0, Agent-as-a-Judge and Inspect Scout are MIT, and Docent and Harbor are Apache-2.0. AI Scientist and DeepReviewer use custom licenses, and the MAST and AIScientistPitfalls repositories have no license file; check the terms before reuse.

**The acceptance gates are the same for every head.** First, directed response: damage aimed at this head must move it in the right direction at every level, and more at higher levels. Second, specificity: damage not aimed at it must not move it by more than the re-judging noise; this ensures the heads measure different things. Third, resolving power: on the same batch of papers, the between-paper standard deviation divided by the re-judging standard deviation must be at least 2; this is the M4 gate of #279, and the pairwise judge is currently at 5.24. Fourth, agreement between the two judges: for code-comparison heads, at least 90% same category, as #377 requires; for heads where the model gives findings, report Cohen's κ by type. Fifth, precision: for each new model head, sample 30 flags for manual checking; at least 24 must hold. This is the standard #377 already set for number verification. Sixth, it read what it should read: every head records which pages and which files it read, and if it did not read everything it records a read failure instead of giving a verdict; this extends the `pages_seen` check of pairsort to all heads. AstaBench's Faker suggests a cheap addition: test with a paper written straight from the task description without running experiments; it should fail every gate and lose every pairwise comparison. This needs no new system runs.

**Resolving power comes from the number of claims and tasks.** One paper has dozens to over a hundred numbers and claims; across 10 tasks, each system has several hundred statistical units. Aggregation uses a bootstrap with tasks as clusters, paired comparison within a task, and a sign test across tasks; the project's existing rule is p = 0.03 when 6 tasks point the same way. Pass conditions do not enter the score. Failing cells are marked separately, and the maintainer decides whether to exclude them; METR's practice is to exclude runs that successfully exploited loopholes from capability results ([METR](https://metr.org/blog/2025-06-05-recent-reward-hacking/)).

**The cross-family problem is handled mainly by code and style swaps.** Code-comparison heads are by nature unaffected by family preference. The comparison head keeps two judges, Claude and GPT, and cross-family conclusions are reported only when both agree. To break down the GPT judge's shift, do a style swap: take one paper, have a Claude model and a GPT model each rewrite the main text, leaving numbers, figures and tables unchanged, recompile, and have both judges judge the pair. If a judge consistently favors its own family's rewrite, the size of that shift is its family shift. If a third opinion is wanted, add a judge from a third family on a subset.

The following are not adopted:

| Not adopted | Reason | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Absolute review scores as the main score (AI Scientist reviewer, DeepReviewer, MLR-Judge overall score) | Scores bunch together; switching judges changes them by nearly 2 points; the same judge differs by 0.68 between two reports; fooled by packaging; we measured only 3 and 4 | Agents4Science; DeepScientist and Jr. AI Scientist; BadScientist |
| A separate idea head, or judging novelty by literature search | Tasks come from published papers, so search finds the original; scores before execution flip after execution; AI Scientist's novelty check has κ of only 0.05 | Ideation–Execution Gap; MLRC-Bench; Idea Novelty Checker |
| Re-running code for full reproduction | Our systems really ran the code; 85.9% of result fabrications can be seen statically from the stored logs; one PaperBench rollout costs about $400, and the code-only variant correlates only weakly with full reproduction | FabScore; PaperBench |
| Counting step-level failure attribution in the score | Joint accuracy 0.183 and 0.050, step-level 14.2%, judges agree on the first error step in only 21/57 cases | TRAIL; Who&When; arXiv 2610.17633 |
| Stability metrics that depend on repeated runs | The design does not repeat runs; claims and tasks are the statistical units instead | τ-bench; arXiv 2602.16666 |
| Self-play Elo, venue acceptance, comparison by showcase papers | Not on the same yardstick; all are hand-picked single outputs | AI co-scientist; AI Scientist v2; Jr. AI Scientist |
| Paper-only error detectors as a scoring head | Recall ≤21% on real errata; different runs find different errors | SPOT; FLAWS |
| Volume as quality (lines of code, papers read, messages) | Volume is not quality; multi-role systems naturally have more messages | Kosmos; MAST |
| Combining the evidence heads into one pairwise verdict by a fixed rule | In #304 this agreed with the maintainer 0/6 | Our measurement |
| Mixing raw scores from different judges, or averaging findings that carry a severity | Judges have systematic offsets from each other; ARA's mean ignored fatal problems | Agents4Science; ARA |
| FabScore as a graded measure | Saturates at 0.998–1.0 on honest systems | Our measurement |

Four gaps must be filled by us; the literature has no ready evidence for them. First, there is no validated automatic detector for "does the gain exceed noise", number of seeds, or fairness of tuning. Second, no one has reported the precision of ARA L2-style claim review. Third, no study has unified our three kinds of logs to compare systems. Fourth, the mutual preferences of GPT and Claude on research papers have never been quantified. Evidence for these four can only come from the known-answer acceptance above, so the acceptance results themselves should go into the evaluator's README and the methods section of the paper.

## Conclusion

For systems that honestly run code, the focus of evaluation should move from "are the numbers real" to "is the evidence enough to support the scope of the claim". The first question is already saturated on our systems: FabScore is 0.998–1.0, and every system really ran its code. The second question is exactly where review comments actually separate systems: gains within noise, small models, few datasets, missing strong baselines. Most of it can be extracted by a model first and then computed by code. A side benefit of this is often overlooked: the comparison rules do not change with the judge, so problems like the GPT judge pushing cross-family disagreements toward GPT papers cannot arise on these heads by construction; only the comparison head still needs judges from two families and style-swap controls.

The literature has no precedent for our kind of comparison, and ResearchClawBench, which tested the same systems, never validated its judge. So whether this evaluator can be trusted depends on how it performs on known answers, not on whose methods it cites. Every head must meet directed response, specificity, resolving power, two-judge agreement, precision and full reading of inputs, and the acceptance numbers must be published together with the results. Only then does the claim "one run separates the systems" have evidence behind it; this evidence can also become part of the paper.

defects.title: 试跑全部失败也继续往下走
defects.title_en: The pipeline continues after every trial run failed
defects.text: CodeAgent 的 exec-fix 循环用无参数、60 秒超时试跑生成的代码；全部迭代都崩溃时流程照样继续，把没跑通过的代码交给后面的阶段。阶段一 ARC-sol 的 10 道里有 7 道如此（t03 t06 t09 t10 a01 r02 r03）。
defects.text_en: CodeAgent's exec-fix loop runs the generated code once per iteration with no arguments and a 60-second timeout; when every iteration crashes the pipeline carries on anyway and hands code that never ran to the later stages. 7 of the 10 phase 1 ARC-sol tasks went this way (t03 t06 t09 t10 a01 r02 r03).

defects.title: 审查改写后的代码不再试跑
defects.title_en: Code rewritten by review is not run again
defects.text: Review 和后续的 Stage 10 改写会替换代码，最终代码在 Stage 12 之前从未执行过。例：t07 的最终代码新增了必填的 --config，Stage 12 以无参数运行即失败。
defects.text_en: Review and the later Stage 10 rewrites replace the code, so the final code is never executed before Stage 12. Example: the final code of t07 gained a required --config, and Stage 12, which runs it without arguments, failed at once.

defects.title: Stage 12 失败即终止，修复环节用不上
defects.title_en: A Stage 12 failure ends the run; the repair step never gets a chance
defects.text: Stage 12 拒绝零指标结果；修复循环只在 Stage 14 之后运行，所以 repair.enabled / max_cycles 对 Stage 12 的失败不起作用。阶段一 ARC-sol 的 10 道都以 Stage 12 “零真实指标”终止。
defects.text_en: Stage 12 refuses a result with zero metrics; the repair loop only runs after Stage 14, so repair.enabled and max_cycles have no effect on a Stage 12 failure. All 10 phase 1 ARC-sol tasks ended at Stage 12 with zero real metrics.

defects.title: 只禁止部分参数
defects.text: 提示词说明运行方式是无参数的 python main.py，但只点名禁止 --condition / --method；也没有任何静态检查拦下必填参数或子命令。阶段一 ARC-sol 有 5 道因此失败（t06 t07 t09 a01 a06）。
defects.text_en: The prompt says the program is run as a bare python main.py but names only --condition and --method as forbidden, and no static check stops a required argument or subcommand. 5 phase 1 ARC-sol tasks failed this way (t06 t07 t09 a01 a06).

defects.title: 文件解析回退把非代码块当作 main.py
defects.title_en: The file-parsing fallback takes a non-code block for main.py
defects.text: _extract_multi_file_blocks 把没有标注文件名的块当作 main.py。例：a01、r03 的 main.py 内容是 filename:requirements.txt 之类；试跑的 stub 也可能被判为“能运行”（t07）。
defects.text_en: _extract_multi_file_blocks takes a block with no file name for main.py. Example: the main.py of a01 and r03 holds text such as filename:requirements.txt; a trial-run stub can also be judged runnable (t07).

defects.title: 依赖扫描把标准库写进 requirements
defects.title_en: The dependency scan writes standard-library modules into requirements
defects.text: _detect_pip_packages 用正则收集 import，只按手写的 _BUILTIN_PACKAGES 跳过，漏掉 __future__、builtins、traceback、importlib 等；一行无效就让 pip 整体安装失败，真正的额外依赖也装不上；上游 entrypoint 把 pip 输出 | tail -20，失败被隐藏。阶段一这 10 道的失败都发生在用到缺失包之前，所以这一条不是决定因素。2026-11-07 复核：阶段一 ARC-sol 的 10 个运行，第 12 阶段的 pip 输出全部有 ERROR（9 个是 Invalid requirement: '__future__'，t02 是 No matching distribution found for builtins）；a06 还把 docstring 里一行 from explicit finite laws… 当成 import，写进了 explicit。在 ARC 镜像里调用 _detect_pip_packages 扫描一个只有 import 语句的文件，返回 __future__、builtins、traceback、fractions、numbers、gzip、importlib、resource；在实验镜像里 pip install -r 含 builtins 的清单退出码为 1、一个包都不装，set -e 下 pip … | tail -20 照样继续（PIPESTATUS 1 0）。10 个运行里只有 t03 的清单含镜像缺少的包（xgboost），t03 在用到它之前就因缺 experiment.json 失败；全部产物中没有 No module named。镜像文件与上游该 commit 的 docker_sandbox.py、entrypoint.sh 的 sha256 一致。
defects.text_en: _detect_pip_packages collects imports with a regular expression and skips only those in a hand-written _BUILTIN_PACKAGES, missing __future__, builtins, traceback, importlib and others; one invalid line makes the whole pip install fail so the real extra dependencies are not installed either, and the upstream entrypoint pipes pip's output through tail -20, which hides the failure. The failures of these 10 phase 1 tasks all happened before a missing package would have been used, so this one was not decisive. Rechecked 2026-11-07: in all 10 phase 1 ARC-sol runs the stage 12 pip output has an ERROR (9 Invalid requirement: '__future__', t02 No matching distribution found for builtins); a06 also took a docstring line from explicit finite laws... for an import and wrote explicit. Calling _detect_pip_packages in the ARC image on a file of import statements returns __future__, builtins, traceback, fractions, numbers, gzip, importlib and resource; in the experiment image pip install -r on a list with builtins exits 1 and installs nothing, and under set -e pip ... | tail -20 carries on (PIPESTATUS 1 0). Of the 10 runs only t03's list holds a package the image lacks (xgboost), and t03 failed on a missing experiment.json before using it; no artifact contains No module named. The image's docker_sandbox.py and entrypoint.sh match the upstream files of that commit by sha256.

defects.title: 不记录实验容器退出码
defects.title_en: The experiment container's exit code is not recorded
defects.text: t10 跑了 574 秒、写出 5229 个结果文件后非零退出，stdout / stderr 都为空；ARC 不保存退出码，原因无法判断。
defects.text_en: t10 ran 574 seconds, wrote 5229 result files and exited non-zero with empty stdout and stderr; ARC does not keep the exit code, so the cause cannot be told.

defects.title: 各阶段的 max_tokens 在上游写死，没有配置项
defects.title_en: Each stage's max_tokens is hard-coded upstream, with no setting
defects.text: Anthropic 路线上各阶段发给模型的 max_tokens 写在上游代码里：代码代理的蓝图 8192，单次代码生成 8192，修复 16384，其余阶段 4096、8192 或 16384；没有配置项可改。只有 gpt-5、o3、o4 开头的模型名会把代码阶段抬到 16384，Claude 不在内。Codex 路线上 codex-api 把 ARC 发的 max_output_tokens 去掉，没有这个上限，所以 ARC-sonnet 比 ARC-sol 多受一层截断：2026-11-02、03 的 ARC-sonnet 运行（思考已关闭）里，多文件代码和论文文本在这些上限处被截断（t06 完成的运行论文正文只有 695 字，草稿 1590 字；t07、a06 第 10 阶段题目一致性检查失败时 12/27、9/30 个请求恰好在上限）。适配层的 max_tokens_floor（默认 32768，只在 Messages API 路线且思考关闭时经补丁抬高 max_tokens）让两条路线的输出上限一致，不改 ARC 的方法（维护者 2026-11-10 决定保留，#303）；这些格子尚未在新设置下重跑。
defects.text_en: On the Anthropic route the max_tokens each stage sends to the model is written in upstream's code: the code agent's blueprint 8192, the single-shot code generation 8192, repairs 16384, the other stages 4096, 8192 or 16384; no setting changes them. Only a model name starting with gpt-5, o3 or o4 lifts the code stages to 16384, and Claude is not among them. On the Codex route codex-api removes the max_output_tokens ARC sends, so there is no such limit, and ARC-sonnet is cut off more often than ARC-sol: in the ARC-sonnet runs of 2026-11-02 and 03 (thinking off) multi-file code and paper text were cut off at these limits (the completed t06 run has a paper body of only 695 words against a draft of 1590; when the stage 10 topic-experiment alignment check failed on t07 and a06, 12 of 27 and 9 of 30 requests ended exactly at the limit). The adapter's max_tokens_floor (default 32768, raising max_tokens through a patch only on the Messages API route with thinking off) makes the output limit of the two routes equal and does not change ARC's method (the maintainer decided on 2026-11-10 to keep it, #303); these cells have not been rerun under the new settings.

defects.title: 蓝图在 8192 处被截断，退回的单次生成缺最后一个文件
defects.title_en: The blueprint is cut off at 8192 and the single-shot fall-back lacks the last file
defects.text: 代码代理的蓝图请求（max_tokens 8192）在上限处被截断，输出以未闭合的 ```yaml 开头，YAML 解析失败；ARC 退回单次代码生成（同样 8192），生成的最后一个文件（含 main.py 的真实驱动）缺失，main.py 成了 config.py 或 data.py 的近似副本（同文档串、同末行）；试跑几毫秒就“能运行”，第 12 阶段 0.02–1.3 s、零指标。2026-11-02、03 的 5 个 ARC-sonnet 运行（思考已关闭，记了 thinking_tokens 的请求全为 0）里，25–32 个请求中 9–16 个的 output_tokens 恰好等于上限。ARC 不保存原始的单次生成响应，这条链由蓝图、main.py 内容和用量日志的对应关系得出；没有在新设置下重跑过，不能说 max_tokens_floor 已使这些格子通过。
defects.text_en: The code agent's blueprint request (max_tokens 8192) is cut off at the limit, the output starts with an unclosed ```yaml and the YAML does not parse; ARC falls back to single-shot code generation (also 8192), whose last file (the one with main.py's real driver) is missing, so main.py is a near copy of config.py or data.py (same docstring, same last line); the trial run "runs" in milliseconds and stage 12 takes 0.02 to 1.3 s with zero metrics. In the 5 ARC-sonnet runs of 2026-11-02 and 03 (thinking off; every request that logged thinking_tokens shows 0), 9 to 16 of 25 to 32 requests ended with output_tokens exactly at the limit. ARC does not keep the raw single-shot response, so the chain follows from the blueprint, the content of main.py and the usage log; it has not been rerun under the new settings, and it cannot be said that max_tokens_floor makes these cells pass.

defects.title: 模型写的 main.py 要求一个 ARC 从不运行的准备步骤
defects.title_en: The model-written main.py needs a preparation step ARC never runs
defects.text: ARC 只以无参数的 python main.py 运行生成的实验（entrypoint 末行 exec python3 -u main.py），没有任何前置步骤，提示词也只禁止 --condition / --method，没有静态检查拦下对前置文件的依赖。冒烟里 ARC-sol（autoresearchclaw-s00-20261110T210743Z）的 main.py 在入口处调 read_constraints，要求同目录的 constraints_ack.json，其中的哈希和 reviewed 标记只能由模型自己写的 prepare_constraints.py 在人工确认后写出（必填 --reviewed-by 等参数，还要交互输入 REVIEWED）；ARC 的流程里没有这一步，门永远过不了，第 12 阶段 5.2 s 零指标（Run status: incomplete，ValueError Constraints review failed closed），第 10 阶段试跑也因同一个门崩溃（rc=1）。题面文件在实验容器里是适配层的只读挂载，宿主侧副本里的 0 字节文件只是挂载点残影，与失败无关。与 only-some-arguments-forbidden 同族：模型写的程序依赖 ARC 不提供的输入。
defects.text_en: ARC runs the generated experiment only as a bare python main.py (the entrypoint's last line is exec python3 -u main.py), with no step before it, the prompt forbids only --condition / --method, and no static check stops a dependency on a prerequisite file. In the smoke, the main.py of ARC-sol (autoresearchclaw-s00-20261110T210743Z) calls read_constraints at its entry and needs a constraints_ack.json beside it, whose hashes and reviewed flag only the model's own prepare_constraints.py writes after a human confirmation (required --reviewed-by and other arguments, plus an interactive REVIEWED); ARC's pipeline has no such step, so the gate can never pass, and stage 12 ended in 5.2 s with zero metrics (Run status: incomplete, ValueError Constraints review failed closed), the stage 10 trial run having crashed on the same gate (rc=1). In the experiment container the task files are the adapter's read-only mounts; the 0-byte files in the host-side copy are only mount-point remnants and unrelated to the failure. Same family as only-some-arguments-forbidden: the model-written program depends on an input ARC does not provide.

defects.title: 修复的整文件重写被 max_tokens 截断，回退把第一个文件当作 main.py
defects.title_en: A repair's full-file rewrite is cut off by max_tokens and the fall-back takes the first file for main.py
defects.text: 第 10 阶段的深度质量检查发现问题（如 config.py 与 pip 包同名）后，让模型“返回完整的修正文件”，用 _extract_multi_file_blocks 解析，结果里有 main.py 就整体采用并写盘。这个整体重写的响应可能在 max_tokens 处被截断：只匹配有闭合围栏的块，截断处之后的文件（含真正的 main.py）被丢弃；没有 main.py 时 _extract_multi_file_blocks 把解析出的第一个文件改名成 main.py。冒烟里 ARC-sonnet（autoresearchclaw-s00-20261110T223856Z）的重写响应以 stop_reason max_tokens（32768 个输出 token）结束，模型把 config.py 改名 experiment_config.py 并第一个输出，于是只有常量、NumericalError、Timer 的文件成了入口 main.py，data.py 里 from experiment_config import * 指向目录里不存在的模块；第 12 阶段运行它是退出码 0、无任何输出，报零指标。ARC 不保存原始响应，这条链是由文件时间戳、用量日志里的 stop_reason 和上游解析规则推出的。属于 blueprint-truncated-at-8192 同族（截断加 main.py 回退），走的是深度质量修复而不是蓝图或单次生成；抬高 max_tokens_floor 能降低概率、不能消除，是否改变设置待维护者定。
defects.text_en: When stage 10's deep quality check finds a problem (such as config.py sharing a name with a pip package) ARC asks the model to "return the complete corrected files", parses the reply with _extract_multi_file_blocks and, if the result has a main.py, adopts the whole set and writes it to disk. The reply to such a full rewrite can be cut off at max_tokens: only blocks with a closed fence match, so the files after the cut (the real main.py among them) are dropped, and when there is no main.py _extract_multi_file_blocks renames the first parsed file to main.py. In the smoke, the rewrite reply of ARC-sonnet (autoresearchclaw-s00-20261110T223856Z) ended with stop_reason max_tokens (32768 output tokens); the model had renamed config.py to experiment_config.py and output it first, so a file with only constants, NumericalError and Timer became the entry point main.py, and data.py's from experiment_config import * points at a module that is not in the directory; stage 12 ran it with exit code 0 and no output at all and reported zero metrics. ARC keeps no raw response; the chain is inferred from file timestamps, the stop_reason in the usage log and upstream's parsing rules. It belongs to the family of blueprint-truncated-at-8192 (truncation plus the main.py fall-back), through the deep quality repair instead of the blueprint or the single-shot generation; raising max_tokens_floor lowers the odds without removing them, and whether to change the setting is for the maintainer to decide.

method.model: Bradley-Terry fitted by the MM algorithm over all decided pairs of all tasks; equal counts 0.5 for each side; prior 0.5 pseudo-win and 0.5 pseudo-loss against a virtual average opponent per condition; log strengths centred to mean 0 (at most 2000 iterations, stop below 1e-10)
method.bootstrap: 1000 resamples of the 10 tasks with replacement, seed 304
method.split_half: 1000 random splits of the tasks into 5 and 5, seed 305
